comments.content: The documented contract on the new `KomiButton` params says "Both must be given together; a partial pair is ignored", and `ClassicButton` implements exactly that (`overrideColors` is only built when both are specified). `MangaButton` instead applies each override independently, so behaviour now differs per personality: passing only `containerColor` silently changes the Manga button (while Classic ignores it), and because the content colour is still derived from the *variant* (`mangaButtonContent`, which resolves contrast against the variant's own container, e.g. `colors.primary` for `Primary`), a partial override can leave unreadable/invisible text. Apply the pair-or-nothing rule here too.

comments.content: Three `Sm` buttons are forced into a single non-wrapping `Row`. `KomiText` label rendering uses `maxLines = 1` + `TextOverflow.Ellipsis` (KomiButton.kt:377-384), so with the newly localized labels this will truncate on narrow dialogs — e.g. ru: "Сначала удалить" + "Всё равно установить" + "Отмена" needs roughly 360dp of button width, while a classic `AlertDialog` on a 360dp screen leaves only ~256dp for the button row. Result: squashed/ellipsized labels such as "Сначала уд…". Consider a wrapping container (e.g. `FlowRow`), or placing Cancel on its own row and the two choices below, or shortening the labels.

comments.content: Returning `false` unconditionally here also discards genuinely numeric evidence. `cmp` is a raw string comparison only when neither side parses; this path is also reached when both sides parse but one is not in `allReleases` and `detectScheme` reported `Unknown`. Concrete case: candidate `2.0.2` (a live tag) vs installed `Alpha4.7.4` whose tag has since been deleted — `cmp` is a real semver compare (`compareNormalized("2.0.2", "4.7.4") == -1`, i.e. 2.0.2 is older), the release list can't order the pair because `currentIndex == -1`, so this now returns `false` and the genuine downgrade is no longer reported. The caller then just attempts the install and the user gets the platform's raw failure message (`installError = t.message`) instead of the downgrade dialog with "Uninstall first" / "Install anyway". The new tests only cover the string-compare case (`2.0.2` vs `nightly`, `dev-5` vs `R2024-01`), so this path is untested. Suggest falling back to `false` only when the comparison was a raw string compare (both normalized versions unparseable) and keeping `cmp < 0` when both normalize to parseable versions.

comments.content:
This new path installs an older release **over an already installed app**, but it still goes through `install()`'s fresh-install branch: `installAsset(...)` is invoked without `isUpdate`, so it keeps its `false` default. Downstream that means `validateApk(isUpdate = false, ...)` skips the package-name mismatch guard (so an APK of another package would be installed silently) and `saveInstalledAppToDatabase` takes the `saveNewInstalledApp` path (a `REPLACE` upsert) instead of `updateInstalledAppVersion` — resetting `installedAt`, `updateCheckEnabled`, the per-app `includePreReleases` setting and clearing the latest-version fields on an app that is only being downgraded.

Before this change a downgrade could only be installed after an uninstall, so `isUpdate = false` was correct there; now it is not. Suggest threading the flag, e.g. `install(ignoreDowngrade = true, isUpdate = installedApp != null)` (or derive it inside `install()` from `_state.value.installedApp`).
comments.thinking:
Confirmed: AndroidInstaller.install launches an ACTION_VIEW intent for the APK; the system installer will refuse a downgrade (shows "App not installed"). And it always returns DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM, so the ViewModel writes the DB as if the install were underway (`isPendingInstall = true`) and logs "Installed". Since the ViewModel can't know the outcome, this is inherent.

OK, decision time. Given the confirmed findings list and the requirement to add value, I'll report:

Comment A (DetailsViewModel, `install(ignoreDowngrade = true)`): the downgrade install is treated as a brand-new install downstream (`isUpdate = false` default in `installAsset`), so the installed record is overwritten via `saveNewInstalledApp` (resetting `installedAt`, per-app `includePreReleases`, `updateCheckEnabled`, clearing latest-version info) instead of `updateInstalledAppVersion`, and the `isUpdate`-gated package-mismatch validation is skipped.
